campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a new interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, along with public hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permits for two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application for public works funding and approving consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation, replacing a prior interim ordinance
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization for the Public Works Director to submit a One Bay Area Grant application
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — June 3, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered options for law enforcement service levels proposed by the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office for the upcoming fiscal year. Council members were asked to direct staff on which service level option to pursue as the city's near-term approach to Sheriff's services.
keyTopics: Selection among Sheriff's Office service level options for FY 2026-27
Direction to staff on the city's near-term approach to Sheriff services

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up a mix of routine business and a few substantive items, including monthly financial reporting, a professional services agreement, and updates to the Town Code through an omnibus ordinance. The Council also considered appointing delegates for an upcoming League of California Cities event and weighed whether to continue or hear a pending appeal at a public hearing.
keyTopics: Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026
Agreement for professional services and a second amendment to an existing agreement
Omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code
Appointment of voting delegate and alternate for the League of California Cities Annual meeting
Request to continue or proceed with a public hearing on pending appeals

san-jose.title: San José City Council — August 25, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council considered routine approval of past Council and Committee meeting minutes, along with expanding the San José Clean Energy SJ Cares program, increasing funding for the Portuguese Organization for Social Services and Opportunities, and amending the City's pay plan.
keyTopics: Expansion of the San José Clean Energy SJ Cares program
Funding increase for the Portuguese Organization for Social Services and Opportunities
Amendment to the City Pay Plan
Approval of City Council meeting minutes
Approval of Council Committee meeting minutes

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council held a regular session that began with public comment on topics not otherwise on the agenda, followed by closed-door discussions. In closed session, the Council considered performance evaluations of its two direct appointees—the City Clerk and City Manager—and met with its labor negotiator regarding compensation for those unrepresented positions.
keyTopics: Public comment period for non-agenda items
Performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiations discussion for unrepresented City Clerk and City Manager positions

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a closed session at 4:30 p.m. followed by a special 6 p.m. meeting featuring a presentation on the CleanWater Program update. The agenda did not include regular business items beyond these two components.
keyTopics: Closed session (special meeting)
Presentation on CleanWater Program update

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event and learn about the Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program. Commissioners also heard from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI and reviewed minutes from their June meeting.
keyTopics: Bike Fest planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program overview
Presentation from youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This was a regular Santa Clara City Council meeting held in a hybrid format, allowing both in-person attendance and remote participation via Zoom or phone. Councilmember Chahal participated remotely from Panchkula, India. The provided agenda materials did not include details on specific policy items considered at this meeting.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format with in-person and Zoom/phone options for public participation

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered introducing an ordinance to amend part of the city's municipal code and received an educational presentation on municipal bonds. The meeting also included routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and reviewing upcoming agenda items.
keyTopics: Ordinance amending Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapters B.6
Presentation on 'Municipal Bonds 101' from Finance staff
Review of the City Council calendar of meetings
Approval of prior City Council meeting minutes
Preview of items planned for the next regular Council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission considered final approval of a public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real private development, with a presentation from the project's art consultant, artist Giles Miller, and the Acclaim Companies development team. The Commission also considered funding for temporary interactive art installations and the acceptance of donated artworks from two local artists.
keyTopics: Final review and approval of public art plan for 3150 El Camino Real development, with presentation by art consultant Danielle Wohl, artist Giles Miller, and Acclaim Companies developers
Allocation of up to $70,000 from the Art in Public Places CIP fund for temporary Code:ART 2027 interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei into the city's public art collection
Approval of June 18, 2026 Public Art Commission meeting minutes
